title: Bounded public release assurance map

surfaces.description: Primary packaged command-line runtime and launchers
Packaged operator-facing setup and usage guidance

domains.rationale: The public runtime processes project-local state and release evidence, so bounded security review is required.
The public runtime reads project-owned files and must preserve its declared local-first and value-minimizing boundaries.
Operator-facing command output and packaged documentation require a bounded accessibility review.
The packaged runtime claims support for declared Python and operating-system environments.
The public package includes operator installation and first-run instructions that must be exercised.
Existing Forge state may be opened by the new runtime and therefore requires an upgrade-path review.
The release procedure must document how the prior public runtime can be restored without corrupting project state.
The primary CLI entrypoint must execute against the declared exact package in representative environments.
This package is a local CLI distribution and does not itself deploy or operate a hosted production service.

obligations.description: Review the declared runtime and guide surfaces for bounded security release risks.
Verify the documented local-first and evidence-retention boundaries against the packaged runtime.
Review command output and packaged guidance for the declared operator accessibility requirements.
Exercise the exact runtime package across every claimed representative environment.
Follow the packaged first-install instructions from a clean environment and record the evidence.
Open representative prior Forge state with the exact package and verify the declared migration behavior.
Exercise and review the declared restoration path to the prior package without project-state damage.
Execute the primary CLI entrypoint from the exact package and verify the declared bounded behavior.

truth_boundary: This contract proves only declared exact-package surface presence and current package-bound receipts for explicitly classified assurance domains; it cannot discover undeclared surfaces, validate reviewer competence, execute tests, or authorize release.
